newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - April 7.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- LABOUR RULES OUT JOINING EMU IN FIRST WAVE

Labour's shadow foreign secretary Robin Cook has effectively ruled out British participation in a European single currency in the lifetime of the next parliament should Labour win the general election. Speaking on London Weekend Television, Cook outlined Labour's resistance to joining the first wave of monetary union, scheduled for January 1999, and added that this opposition extends to the planned 2002 start-up of full circulation of the euro.
-- NEW LAW 'MAY LEAD TO PENSION SCANDAL'

Experts are warning that new laws on company pension schemes, due to take effect Monday, could fuel a new pensions scandal via a loophole which allows employers to avoid the laws by setting up low-cost schemes the act does not cover. The low-cost group personal pension (GPP) schemes, which are not covered by the new Pensions Act, are likely to give poor benefits to workers who move jobs frequently. Tom Ross, chairman of the National Association of Pension Funds, has warned that 'very positive' steps are needed to avoid another pensions scandal.
-- POWERGEN LETTER DENTS PROFIT HOPES

Analysts are revising downwards their estimates of annual pre-tax profits at electricity generator PowerGen after the company circulated a letter containing what it described as a 'pre-closed season' list of pointers. In the letter, PowerGen highlighted a lower range of 'key analysts' forecasts' and quoted a range of 61p-69.8p for earnings per share and 27.1p to 34.2p for its dividend per share. PowerGen denied it was making a profits forecast with the letter, but one analyst revised his pre-tax profits down from 650 million stg to 580 million stg.
-- PROTEST OVER BT DUTCH VENTURE

Telfort, the Netherlands-based joint venture between British Telecom and the Dutch state-owned railway, has indicated to the Dutch government that it may rethink its investment of more than Fl1 billion (325 million stg) in the Dutch telecoms market because of the way interconnection tariffs are being treated. The company, whose fibre optic cable network, laid alongside rail lines, will be 40 percent complete by the end of the year, feels disadvantaged by the tariffs.
-- BRITISH ENERGY INVESTS IN GAS POWER STATION

Nuclear power group British Energy (BE) is set to make a joint announcement with French energy group Elf on Monday about an investment in its first gas-fired power station. The announcement is expected to concern Humberside power station Humber Power, in which four investors have already taken stakes in the 796 million stg plan to build a power station with capacity of 1,200MW. The move would be in line with BE's intention to diversify into other forms of power generation.
-- OFGAS TO GIVE EVIDENCE TO MMC

The scheduling of a meeting on Monday between gas industry regulator Clare Spottiswoode and the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) has heightened speculation about a report due from the Commission into the prices charged by BG, formerly British Gas GAS.L. The report is expected to be sent to Ofgas next Monday, but the timing of this week's meeting has fueled industry expectation that the MMC is likely to give concessions to both sides in the dispute.
-- MOTORCYCLE SALES SET TO SHOW STRONG GROWTH

Figures due out this week from Motor Cycle Trader, the main journal of the British industry, are expected to show further strong growth in motorcycle sales in March. The growth, which would take the sector's recovery into its third year, is being led by demand for high-powered, expensive sports motorcycles at one end of the market, and the increasing popularity of mopeds and scooters at the other.
-- FLOAT COULD VALUE GLOBAL LINK AT 3.7 BILLION STG

U.S. telecommunications group USA Global Link is planning to float later this year in an IPO which could value the fast-growing company at between 3 billion dollars and 6 billion dollars (1.8 billion stg to 3.7 billion stg). The Iowa-based company, which offers innovative and often controversial ways of cutting the cost of international telephone calls, turns over just under 1 billion dollars a year.
-- MICROSOFT BUYS WEBTV NETWORKS

U.S. software giant Microsoft is to acquire WebTV, a Silicon Valley company which has developed technology to enable consumers to surf the Internet via their TV sets. Microsoft will pay about $425 million (267 million stg) for WebTV, in a move which underscores the U.S. giant's determination to play a leading role in the convergence of personal computing and consumer electronics when digital television transmissions begin in the United States next year.
-- GLAXO HIT BY US RULING ON ZANTAC

British pharmaceuticals giant Glaxo Wellcome has lost a U.S. court case against a competitor who intends producing a generic version of Glaxo's 'blockbuster' ulcer drug, Zantac. The U.S. Court of Appeals ruled on Friday that Canadian drugs company Novopharm can produce its version of Zantac, the world's best-selling medicine, when Glaxo's patent expires at the end of July.
